title: Relative brain microplastic concentration, dementia-diagnosed vs not

source.name: Bioaccumulation of microplastics in decedent human brains (autopsy study)
source.publisher: University of New Mexico Health Sciences (Campen et al.), Nature Medicine

notes: The same study found brain tissue from decedents with a documented dementia diagnosis carried roughly 3 to 5 times the microplastic concentration of brains without such a diagnosis (shown here as an illustrative index, midpoint ~4x). The authors are explicit this shows an association, not proof that microplastics cause dementia — impaired blood-brain-barrier filtering in dementia is a likely factor.
